current_bottleneck: 333b global mixing repaired shared coupling but damaged local path fidelity. The clean read is that the global communication path is useful, but the value interface is too level-only: the model must infer local increments/tails from noised levels, which worsens daily KS, time-series tails, level KS, and worst-cell cointegration.
last_result_summary: Postmortem after 333a/333b: 333a gives better local fidelity and cointegration but fails cross-cell coupling; 333b gives passing cross-cell coupling and much stronger h1 MR but loses daily/level/time-series fidelity. This is a local-vs-global representation tradeoff inside the masked path law, not evidence for temperature/depth tuning.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 333c: keep 333b global scenario mixing and the same masked full-path rectified-flow objective, but feed each token both its standardized logit level and its implied one-step transition. Level and transition are invertible views of the same path, so this is a coordinate/interface repair rather than a residual branch or auxiliary evaluator loss.
current_best_note: 330a and 330c tie the 5/11 frontier with cleaner first-principles autoregressive sequence-density models, without retrieval, low-rank readouts, residual shells, or evaluator-specific losses.
